title: Resilience Playbook — 90 Day Iteration Cookbook & Ops↔Product Handshake
content:
Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable 90-day iteration cookbook that teams can adopt to migrate from ad-hoc reliability fixes to SLO-driven product decisions. Focus is cross-functional: Product, Platform, Serving Runtime, Observability, SRE, and Solutions Eng. This doc is a pragmatic skeleton — runbooks, decision gates, and an operations↔product handshake for incremental SLO rollouts.

Context and why now:
- Multiple teams are launching model-serving features with growing customer SLAs. We lack a unified cadence for SLO discovery, developer-level metrics, and clear rollouts.
- Recent incidents exposed gaps: missing error-budget ownership, inconsistent alert thresholds across teams, poor canary-to-global rollout criteria.

Scope (what this cookbook covers):
- Service selection and SLI discovery (how to pick signals and baseline noise)
- SLO proposal template and lightweight review workflow
- 90-day phased rollout plan (small canary → expanded canary → staged global)
- Handshake checklist for Product ↔ SRE (who signs off and when)
- Runbook handover and oncall readiness criteria
- Observability dashboards, dashboards-as-code snippets, and regression detection signals

Desired outcome / success criteria (end of 90 days):
- 3 customer-facing services onboarded to platform SLOs with documented error budgets and alerting
- Canary-to-global rollout playbook executed once end-to-end
- One post-rollout regression caught by the new dashboards and remediated without customer impact
- SLOs incorporated into product release criteria (PR checklist item)

Primary metrics (what we measure):
- SLO coverage (% of traffic/users under SLOs) — target +20% in 90 days
- Time from SLO proposal to canary (< 30 days target)
- Number of incidents per service month-over-month (trend down)
- Error budget spend rate and alerts triggered (fewer surprise burn events)

Prioritization rubric for services to onboard first:
1) Customer-impact (external-facing latency/accuracy issues)
2) Traffic/scale (top 10 services by qps)
3) Operational pain (flaky, noisy alerts, frequent post-release fixes)
4) Product willingness to pause rollouts if SLO fails

Single-page SLO proposal template (use this as the PR body for SRE review):
- Service name: <service>
- Owner(s): Product eng, Platform, SRE
- Business impact: short paragraph (who is affected and how)
- Key SLIs (1–3): e.g., p50 latency, p95 latency, success-rate per request-type
- Proposed SLO: target and window (e.g., 99.5% success rate over 30d)
- Canary rollout plan: % traffic, burn rate, measurement windows
- Alerting: what alert and to whom (pager, metrics Slack, runbook)
- Rollback criteria: hard thresholds + manual approval path
- Linked dashboards + test queries

Cross-functional roles and compact responsibilities (handshake):
- Product Manager: declares acceptable customer impact, participates in canary sign-off, owns business metrics mapping
- Service/Feature Engineer: implements SLIs and instrumentation, owns initial rollouts and PRs
- Platform/Infra: ensures platform-level metrics (node/capacity), supports safe traffic shifting and reserve capacity
- Observability/Monitoring: builds the dashboards-as-code snippets, sets up burn-rate alerts, implements synthetic checks
- SRE: reviews SLO proposal, validates runbooks, leads oncall training and postmortem cadence
- Solutions Eng/Customer Success: communicates risk windows to customers when needed

90-day phased plan (high-level weeks and milestones):
- Week 0–2: Discovery and SLI baseline
  - Kickoff workshop (30–60 min) with Product + Eng + SRE
  - Run a 7-day traffic/sample collection, document noise and outliers
  - Deliverable: baseline report + proposed SLIs
- Week 3–5: Implement instrumentation + dashboards
  - Merge PRs that emit SLIs to metrics pipeline
  - Observability builds dashboards-as-code and synthetic probes
  - Deliverable: testable canary dashboard + runbook draft
- Week 6–8: Canary (limited traffic)
  - Start canary at 1–5% traffic, measure burn-rate for 48–72h
  - Daily check-ins (15m) with Product and SRE; document anomalies
  - Deliverable: canary sign-off decision (expand, pause, rollback)
- Week 9–11: Staged expansion and platform validation
  - Gradual traffic growth with platform capacity checks and autoscaling validation
  - Validate cost/latency tradeoffs, model quantization effects, etc.
  - Deliverable: expansion decision + runbook updated
- Week 12: Global rollout + retrospective
  - Full traffic shift, monitoring guardrails in place
  - Run a blameless postmortem + improvement action log
  - Deliverable: completion badge + SLO integrated into release checklist

Sprint-level tasks (example backlog items to create in Jira):
- REL-601: Run SLI discovery workshop for payments service (owner: Jonah)
- REL-602: Add request success metric to service A telemetry (owner: service eng)
- OBS-170: Create dashboard snippet and synthetic probe for service A (owner: Sofia)
- SRE-45: Draft runbook and escalation map (owner: Priya)
- PLAT-88: Build traffic-splitting job and throttling guardrail (owner: Michael)

Runbook & oncall readiness checklist (must be satisfied before canary):
- Runbook written and committed (path + link)
- Page-cards created and tested (no missing runbook steps)
- Oncall rotation notified and 2 responders trained on runbook in a 30m dry-run
- Synthetic canary probe in place; warm-up traffic validated
- Rollback play tested in staging (last-resort path documented)

Guardrails and decision gates (binary checks to move forward):
- SLI telemetry completeness >= 95% (no major gaps)
- Observability dashboard refresh < 60s for p95 queries
- Error budget burn-rate below threshold during canary window (configurable)
- Product approves customer-impact tradeoffs in writing

Communication plan (who, when, how):
- Pre-canary: announcement to #sre-ops + #product-launch 48h before
- Daily during canary: 15m async status notes in thread + short standup if triggered
- Major escalation: PagerDuty page and dedicated war-room channel
- Post-release summary: 1 pager to execs and stakeholders with metrics and next steps

Observability patterns (templates):
- Dashboard page: summary tile (SLO burn %), service health (success-rate p50/p95), latency histograms, error taxonomy heatmap
- Burn-rate detector: rolling-window derivative on error-rate + weighted impact by user cohort
- Canary synthetic: sequence of requests that validate correctness + latency SLA

Risk register (top risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Insufficient instrumentation —> Mitigation: Blocker gate, pair-program with Observability
- Risk: Canary traffic diverges from real traffic pattern —> Mitigation: Use production-weighted synthetic cohorts and stage expansion slowly
- Risk: Auto-scaling lags and causes timeouts —> Mitigation: Platform pre-warm and capacity reservations for rollout windows
- Risk: Product pushes to expand despite burn —> Mitigation: Signed rollback authority rests with SRE lead for safety

Training & enablement:
- 60–90 minute workshop for engineers: SLI design patterns and dashboard debugging (deliverable: slide deck + lab exercises)
- 30 minute onboarding for Product managers: mapping product impact to SLO language and decision rules
- Cheatsheet: 1-page SLO design rules + common pitfalls (put in Confluence and link in PR template)

Post-rollout play and continuous improvement:
- 30/60/90 day check-ins to validate SLOs still reflect user experience
- Maintain a lightweight experiment log: what changes were made, unit economics impact, and quality regressions
- Quarterly SLO tuning session across product areas to consolidate learnings

Open questions / decisions to resolve early:
- Window sizing: 30d vs 7d — recommendation: default 30d for availability/quality, 7d for very-labile metrics
- Ownership model for multi-tenant features — split error budgets per tenant or global? Proposal: global default with per-tenant alerting for high-value customers
- Cost visibility during canary — need a live cost dashboard for tokenized model serving (PLAT ticket)

Next steps (immediate actions):
- Book kickoff (owners: Aisha + Jonah) and invite Product, Observability, Platform leads — target: within 3 business days
- Create canonical SLO proposal PR template in the repo (owner: Sofia)
- Spin up initial pilot service candidate list and schedule discovery workshops

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally procedural and rollout-focused (not academic). We want something teams can copy-paste and iterate.
- Please add missing step items or blockers as comments in the Confluence page linked above.

- [ ] Finalize canary traffic tooling (PLAT-88)

- [ ] Schedule training workshop and record session (SRE-45)
